definitions.gloss: owner; master; the person a thing belongs to
definitions.explanation: The person who owns or is responsible for something. On its own it is somewhat old-fashioned, but it is extremely productive as a suffix: {世帯主|せたいぬし} (head of household), {持|も}ち{主|ぬし} (owner), {飼|か}い{主|ぬし} (pet owner), {貸|か}し{主|ぬし} (lender).

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{財布|さいふ}→財布：00663_saifu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{主|ぬし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{探|さが}している→探す：00493_sagasu⟧。
examples.english: I'm looking for the owner of this wallet.

examples.japanese: ⟦{住民票|じゅうみんひょう}→住民票：09628_juuminhyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{世帯主|せたいぬし}→世帯主：15836_setainushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: You write the head of household's name on the residence certificate.

examples.japanese: ⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{飼|か}い{主|ぬし}→飼い主：15281_kainushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{散歩中|さんぽちゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マナー→マナー：11139_manaa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{求|もと}められる→求める：02316_motomeru⟧。
examples.english: Dog owners are expected to have good manners while walking their dogs.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{土地|とち}→土地：02226_tochi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}→持ち主：10439_mochinushi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{分|わ}から→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧ず、⟦{工事|こうじ}→工事：00244_kouji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{進|すす}められない→進める：01949_susumeru⟧ままだ。
examples.english: The owner of this land is unknown, so the construction work still can't move forward.

notes:
The same kanji read あるじ means the master of a house or shop; ぬし is the reading used in compounds about ownership.

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{世帯主|せたいぬし}→世帯主：15836_setainushi⟧: head of household (the official term on forms)
- ⟦{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}→持ち主：10439_mochinushi⟧: owner (of an object, land, or vehicle)
- ⟦{飼|か}い{主|ぬし}→飼い主：15281_kainushi⟧: owner of a pet
- ⟦{地主|じぬし}→地主：12048_jinushi⟧: landowner, landlord
- {落|お}とし{主|ぬし}: the person who dropped something

USAGE:
Standalone {主|ぬし} sounds literary or archaic today; in modern speech people say ⟦{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}→持ち主：10439_mochinushi⟧ or ⟦オーナー→オーナー：10830_oonaa⟧ instead. In folklore, the {主|ぬし} of a lake or forest is its guardian spirit — a large old animal said to rule the place.
